rail_guard.text: Waverley Station, the only station in the world named after a novel. It's named after Sir Walter Scott's 'Waverley'. The trains are not obliged to be as long.
Hop aboard! The Wildlore rail runs to every station you've visited in Great Britain. Where to?

then.text: There's a ceilidh tonight. I'm told I dance like a shopping trolley with a wonky wheel. I've been practising on the cobbles. The pigeons are unimpressed.
You go on ahead. I'll catch you up. Probably. If there's a scone.
The Castle Esplanade: cobbles, a crowd, and the Castle itself standing on its black rock like a very old cat on a very tall fence. Kit is sitting on a bollard eating chips with a wooden fork.
{player}! Edinburgh Castle! I've been up and down the Royal Mile three times. My legs have filed a complaint.
Seven Stones each... wait, you've got more than me. Typical. One more go, for old times' sake?

else.text: I'll tell you what, though. Standing up here, looking out at the whole city, I remembered why I started. Not the likes. Just the walking.
Strachan's up in the Highlands, apparently. Waxed jacket, clipboard. She has a lanyard that makes Kerrigan's look casual. Be careful.

edi_guide.text: The Castle's on a volcanic plug. A big old volcano chilled out about 340 million years ago, and the glaciers scraped it into a crag with a long tail. Hence 'Crag and Tail'.
The One O'Clock Gun goes off at one o'clock. It started in 1861 so ships in the Forth could set their clocks. Now it startles tourists. A fine tradition.

edi_fringe.text: In August the Fringe takes over the whole city: thousands of shows, a few hundred of them with real audiences, and one with a very committed accordion.
It's the biggest arts festival in the world. I'm doing a comedy set about pigeons. It's called 'Squab Goes Hungry'. Come on Tuesday. There'll be a seat.

edi_gardener.text: The Floral Clock's a proper working clock and, I'll have you know, the oldest in the world. It's all planted in spring. It takes a month and a lot of kneeling.
Mind the daffs. Children can walk on the daffs, but only after school.

edi_walker.text: Arthur's Seat is an extinct volcano with a nice view and a path. You can be on top of it in an hour, and you will want a scone afterwards.
They say King Arthur sat there, but there's no real evidence. There's a lot of evidence for seagulls.
